experiments.name: Trend following (10-month SMA)
experiments.hypothesis: Bear markets tend to start below a slow moving average; stepping aside cuts the deepest drawdowns.
rules: Hold S&P 500 when month-end price > 10-month SMA

experiments.name: Time-series momentum (12-month)
experiments.hypothesis: Trailing 12-month excess return persists for months (under-reaction, slow capital flows).
rules: Hold equities when trailing 12m total return > cash return

experiments.name: Mean reversion (buy after -5% month, hold 3)
experiments.hypothesis: Sharp monthly declines overshoot and partially reverse.
rules: After a month with price return <= -5%, hold equities 3 months

experiments.name: Trend + calm-volatility override
experiments.hypothesis: Whipsaws happen when vol is low; stay invested in calm markets even below trend.
rules: Invested if price > 10m SMA OR 12m realized vol < 20%

experiments.name: Volatility targeting (15%)
experiments.hypothesis: Risk clusters; scaling exposure down when realized vol is high improves risk-adjusted return.

experiments.name: Valuation timing (CAPE vs. 20y median)
experiments.hypothesis: Expensive markets deliver lower forward returns, so step out when CAPE is far above its own history.
rules: Invested when CAPE <= 1.2x its trailing 20-year median

experiments.name: Value + trend (either signal)
experiments.hypothesis: Combine a slow valuation signal with trend so neither alone forces you out.
rules: Invested if price > 10m SMA OR CAPE <= its 20y median

experiments.name: Relative strength: stocks vs. gold (6-month)
experiments.hypothesis: Capital rotates toward the asset with stronger recent performance.
rules: Each month hold whichever of S&P 500 / gold had the higher 6-month return
experiments.note: Gold was fixed before 1971; tested 1971+ only (train 1971-1999, test 2000-2026).

walk_forward.method: Each decade, choose the SMA length with best Sharpe on ALL prior data, then trade it untouched for the next 10 years.

overfitting_demo.lesson: 300 random seasonal rules (hold in 6 random calendar months). The 10 best in training look skilled in training; out-of-sample they fall back toward the average. Selection, not skill.
